name: Basil

basicInfo.description: Sweet basil is one of the easiest herbs to grow. It thrives in warm weather, grows quickly in small spaces, and adds fresh flavor to many dishes.
whyGrow: Adds incredible flavor to pasta, pizza, and salads
Ready to harvest in just 4 weeks
Perfect for small spaces and windowsills
Cheaper than buying fresh basil weekly
basicInfo.sunlight: 4-6 hours of direct sun daily (can grow in partial shade)
basicInfo.water: Keep soil moist but not soggy - water when the top feels dry

growingSteps: Fill a small container (15-20cm deep) with potting mix
Sow seeds 0.5 cm deep or plant seedlings
Place in a sunny windowsill or balcony
Water when soil surface feels dry
Pinch off flower buds to encourage leaf growth
Harvest leaves from the top down, leaving lower leaves
Fertilize lightly every 2 weeks during growing season

careCalendar.description: Check soil every morning. If the top feels dry, add a little water.
Remove weaker sprouts and leave the strongest ones spaced apart.
Pinch top leaves to encourage bushy growth.
Cut a few leaves each week to prevent flowering.
Add diluted liquid fertilizer with water.
Pick leaves as needed. Always cut from the top.

harvestingGuide: Harvest basil leaves when they are large enough to use, about 4-6 weeks after planting. Pinch off individual leaves or cut stems just above a leaf node. Regular harvesting keeps the plant bushy and productive.
estimatedSavings: Growing basil at home can save $40–60 per year, since supermarket bunches cost $3-5 and a single plant produces leaves for months.
